I feel unusually confident, almost invincible, and I’ve blown a lot of money on impulsive investments and luxury stuff I don’t need.

During these times, I also eat in this weird, out‑of‑control way. I’ll order enough room service for three people and just keep going until I feel painfully stuffed. Every so often, maybe once or twice a year for the last few years, I go into these stretches that last about a week where I barely sleep but feel like I don’t need it. I’ll sleep maybe three hours and still be buzzing with energy. My mind races with ideas for work and home, I talk nonstop in meetings, feel incredibly confident, and start big projects—like reorganizing the whole department or planning a new business—without thinking them through. My husband says I get “amped up” and impulsive; I’ll spend a lot on stuff we don’t need and get irritable if anyone slows me down.
